sections.title: Receipt drawer behaviour
sections.what: Checks the receipt drawer opens and closes from the keyboard and button, keeps focus on the toggle after closing, shows the source and model details, and that story receipts list their incident references.
sections.why: Makes the evidence trail usable by keyboard and by people who depend on screen readers.
sections.watch_out: Exact model and attribution wording is hard-coded, so any change to those labels breaks the test.

summary: Browser test of the receipt drawer: it opens and closes by keyboard and button, shows source, time class and attribution, and story receipts list the incidents behind them.
purpose: Confirms every claim can be traced to its source and that the trace works without a mouse.
why: Receipts are how the app shows its evidence, so they must open reliably and show the right details.
how: It opens the Desk, focuses the first receipt toggle, and presses Enter to open it. It checks the drawer names the source, the verification class, the match date and the replay clock note, the attribution line and the model name with its hash. It presses Escape to close and checks focus returns to the toggle, reopens with Space, and closes with the close button. Finally it opens a story receipt and checks it lists its incident references, then runs an accessibility check.
inputs: The Desk page and its first receipt and story receipt.
outputs: Pass or fail for opening, closing, focus and content.
risks: Expected attribution and hash wording are fixed, so changes to those strings break the test.
debug: If focus is lost after closing, check the drawer's focus handling. If content is missing, compare the drawer's fields against the expected text.
